subject: Day 1: Here we go. The story of Jesus starts now.
body:
Good morning.

Today is the day. You are starting the New Testament and I am reading alongside you.

Matthew opens with a genealogy. It might be tempting to skip it. Do not. Because buried in that list of names are Rahab, Ruth, and Bathsheba. Women who should not be in the family tree of the Messiah. But they are. That tells you something about the kind of God we serve.

Then Jesus is born. Then He is baptized. Then He walks into the wilderness for forty days. And then He starts teaching. The Sermon on the Mount begins in chapter 5 and it is some of the most powerful teaching you will ever read.

Nine chapters today. That is it. You can do this.

Heather

subject: Day 2: Miracles and hard questions
body:
Good morning.

Today Jesus sends out the twelve disciples. He feeds thousands with a boy's lunch. He walks on water. Peter tries to walk on water and sinks. And Jesus asks the most important question in the entire Bible. Who do you say that I am?

Peter gets it right. You are the Christ.

That question was not just for Peter. It is for you too. After everything you read yesterday and everything you will read today, the question is the same. Who do you say He is?

You are on Day 2. You showed up again. That is what matters.

Heather

subject: Day 3: The week that changed everything
body:
Good morning.

Today you will read about the rich young ruler, the workers in the vineyard, and Jesus entering Jerusalem on a donkey. Then the tension builds. The last supper. The garden. The betrayal. The cross. The tomb.

And then chapter 28. He is not here. He has risen.

I have read this story many times. It still gets me. Every time.

You just finished your first book of the New Testament. Three days in, one Gospel done. Keep going.

Heather

subject: Day 4: Mark does not slow down
body:
Good morning.

Mark is the shortest Gospel and it moves fast. The word you will see more than any other is immediately. Jesus does this, then immediately does that. Mark does not have time for long speeches. He wants you to see what Jesus did.

You will recognize stories from Matthew. That is okay. Pay attention to what Mark includes that Matthew did not. The details are different. The angle is different.

Mark writes like someone who is in a hurry to tell you the most important story in the world. Let him.

Day 4. You are building momentum.

Heather

subject: Day 5: The cross, again. And it hits different the second time.
body:
Good morning.

You are reading the crucifixion story for the second time in five days. And something strange happens when you read it again this soon. You notice things you missed.

Mark's account is rawer. Shorter. More brutal. And Mark's Gospel originally ended at chapter 16 verse 8. The women at the tomb, trembling and afraid, saying nothing to anyone.

That is a strange way to end a book. Unless the point is that the story is not over. It is your turn now.

Two Gospels done. You are almost a week in.

Heather

subject: Day 6: Luke notices the people nobody else sees
body:
Good morning.

Luke is a doctor. He is detail-oriented. And he cares about people that the other Gospel writers sometimes skip past.

Today you will read about Elizabeth, an older woman who had given up on having children. About shepherds, who were nobodies. About Simeon and Anna, two elderly people waiting in the temple for something they had been promised.

Luke sees the margins. The overlooked. The forgotten. If you have ever felt invisible, Luke's Gospel is for you.

Six days in. You are finding your rhythm.

Heather

subject: Day 7: One week done
body:
Good morning. One full week.

Today you will read some of the most famous stories Jesus ever told. The good Samaritan. Martha and Mary. The Lord's Prayer.

Pause on Martha and Mary for a moment. Martha is doing all the work. Mary is sitting at the feet of Jesus. And Jesus says Mary chose the better thing.

That is hard to hear when you are the one doing all the work. But I think the point is not that doing is wrong. It is that there are moments when the most important thing is to stop and sit.

This might be one of those moments. You have been reading for seven days straight. Take a breath. Sit with what you have read. You are doing so well.

Heather

subject: Day 8: Lost things and found things
body:
Good morning.

Today you will read the prodigal son. Luke 15. It is the most famous parable Jesus ever told and it still wrecks me.

A son takes his inheritance, wastes it, ends up feeding pigs, and comes home expecting to be a servant. And the father runs to him. Does not wait. Does not lecture. Runs.

I have been the prodigal. I have been the older brother too. And the thing that gets me every time is the father. He was watching. He was waiting. He ran.

That is how God feels about you. Right now. Today.

Heather

subject: Day 9: The cross, the third time. What do you see now?
body:
Good morning.

This is the third time you are reading the death and resurrection of Jesus. And I want to ask you something. What are you noticing now that you did not notice the first time?

Luke includes things the others do not. Jesus sweating drops of blood in the garden. Telling the thief on the cross, today you will be with me in paradise. Walking with two disciples on the road to Emmaus after the resurrection, and they did not even recognize Him until He broke bread.

That last one gets me. Sometimes Jesus is right next to you and you do not see it until later.

Three Gospels done. You are almost a third of the way through the New Testament.

Heather

subject: Day 10: John sees something the others did not
body:
Good morning.

John is different. You will feel it immediately.

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

No genealogy. No birth story. John starts before the beginning of time. Because John is not trying to tell you what Jesus did. He is trying to show you who Jesus is.

Today you will read about water turned to wine, Nicodemus coming to Jesus at night, the woman at the well, and Jesus feeding five thousand. But John frames each one as a sign. A glimpse of something bigger.

Ten days in. One third done. You are in this.

Heather

subject: Day 11: I am
body:
Good morning.

Today you will read some of the most powerful words Jesus ever spoke. I am the light of the world. I am the good shepherd. I am the resurrection and the life. I am the way, the truth, and the life.

Every one of those I am statements would have hit the people listening like a thunderbolt. Because they knew that I AM was the name God gave Himself when Moses asked at the burning bush.

Jesus was not being subtle. He was saying exactly who He was.

Chapter 11 is the raising of Lazarus. And right before He does it, Jesus weeps. He already knew He was about to raise His friend from the dead. And He still cried. Because He felt the grief.

That is the kind of God you are reading about.

Heather

subject: Day 12: The upper room and the empty tomb
body:
Good morning.

John 15 through 17 is Jesus talking to His closest friends the night before He dies. And it is the most intimate conversation in the Bible. I am the vine. Abide in me. I call you friends. I am praying for you.

Then the cross. Then the tomb. Then Mary Magdalene in the garden, weeping, and Jesus says her name. Mary. And she knows.

Then Thomas, who doubted, gets to put his hands in the wounds. And Peter, who denied Jesus three times, gets asked three times, do you love me?

Four Gospels done. You have seen Jesus from four angles. Tomorrow the church begins.

Heather

subject: Day 13: The Holy Spirit shows up and everything changes
body:
Good morning.

Jesus ascends. The disciples wait. And then the Holy Spirit falls on them like fire and they start speaking in languages they have never learned and Peter, the man who denied Jesus, stands up and preaches and three thousand people believe.

That is Acts chapter 2. And the rest of the book just keeps going.

Today you will also read about Stephen, the first person killed for following Jesus. His last words were, Lord, do not hold this sin against them. Just like Jesus on the cross.

Acts is the most exciting book in the New Testament. It reads like an adventure story. Because it is one.

Heather

subject: Day 14: Two weeks in. Paul enters the story.
body:
Good morning. Two weeks.

Today a man named Saul, who has been hunting Christians and throwing them in prison, gets knocked off his horse by a blinding light. And Jesus says, Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?

Saul becomes Paul. And the entire trajectory of Christianity changes because of it.

I love this story because it proves that nobody is too far gone. The guy who was the worst enemy of the church became its greatest champion. If God can use Paul, He can use anyone.

You are halfway through the challenge. Fourteen days done. Fourteen to go.

Heather

subject: Day 15: Missionary journeys and midnight worship
body:
Good morning.

Paul is on the move today. City after city. Shipwrecks. Beatings. Prison. And in chapter 16, Paul and Silas are sitting in a jail cell at midnight, bleeding from being beaten, and they start singing.

Singing. In prison. At midnight. After being beaten.

And then an earthquake breaks the chains and the jailer falls to his knees and asks, what must I do to be saved?

That is the power of worship in the dark places. It does not just change you. It changes the people watching.

Fifteen days down. You are in the second half now.

Heather

subject: Day 16: Paul will not stop
body:
Good morning.

Paul gets arrested. Put on trial. Appealed to Caesar. Shipwrecked on the way to Rome. Bitten by a snake on the island. And he just keeps going.

The book of Acts ends with Paul in Rome, under house arrest, still preaching the gospel. Still teaching. Still unhindered.

That is the last word of Acts. Unhindered. The gospel cannot be stopped. Not by chains. Not by storms. Not by snakes. Not by Rome.

You just finished Acts. Tomorrow you start Paul's letters. This is where it gets personal.

Here is my one ask for the second half: tell someone.

Not so you have a buddy to keep you accountable. Tell them because of what this has been for you. If reading the Word this way has meant something, if it has shifted how you see God or how you read the Bible, there is someone in your life who needs that too. Good things are meant to be handed to other people.

You do not even have to find the words. Here is something you can copy, change to sound like you, and post or text to a friend:

"Reading the New Testament in a month has changed how I read it. Not as individual verses and stories, but the big picture. I am halfway through. You can start any day you want. Come do it with me. heatherlynwilson.com/challenge #31DayBibleChallenge"

Post it, text it, drop it in your group chat. Someone else meeting God in His Word could start with your one sentence.

Heather

subject: Day 17: The deepest theology Paul ever wrote
body:
Good morning.

Romans is dense. I am not going to pretend otherwise. Paul is building an argument, brick by brick, about sin and grace and faith and salvation.

But chapter 8 is where it all lands. And chapter 8 might be the single greatest chapter in the entire Bible.

There is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. All things work together for good. Nothing can separate us from the love of God.

If you only remember one chapter from this entire challenge, make it Romans 8.

Seventeen days. You have read more of the Bible than most people read in a lifetime.

Heather

subject: Day 18: Grace changes everything
body:
Good morning.

The second half of Romans shifts from theology to practice. Paul is saying, okay, you understand grace. Now here is what it looks like to live it.

Chapter 12 is one of the most practical chapters in the Bible. Love sincerely. Hate evil. Be joyful in hope. Patient in affliction. Faithful in prayer. Bless those who persecute you. Do not repay evil for evil.

That is not a suggestion. That is what grace looks like when it hits the ground.

Eighteen down. You are in a groove. Keep it.

Heather

subject: Day 19: Paul writes to a messy church
body:
Good morning.

Corinth was a mess. The church was divided. People were suing each other. There were arguments about everything.

And Paul does not start by yelling at them. He starts by reminding them who they are. You are called. You are sanctified. You belong to Christ.

That is always God's approach. Before He corrects you, He reminds you who you are.

Today's reading is Paul dealing with real problems in a real church. It sounds like it could have been written last week. People have not changed much in two thousand years.

Twelve days left.

Heather

subject: Day 20: Love and resurrection
body:
Good morning. Twenty days in.

Today you hit two of the most famous chapters in the Bible. Chapter 13, the love chapter. And chapter 15, the resurrection chapter.

Love is patient. Love is kind. You have heard it before. But read it today as Paul writing to people who were anything but patient and kind. It is not a poem about romance. It is a mirror held up to a church that needed to hear it.

And chapter 15. If Christ has not been raised, your faith is useless. But Christ has been raised. And because He has, everything changes.

Twenty days. Eleven to go. You are so close.

Heather

subject: Day 21: Three weeks. Strength in weakness.
body:
Good morning. Three full weeks.

Second Corinthians is Paul at his most vulnerable. He talks about being crushed. Despairing of life. Carrying the sentence of death within himself.

And then he says this. We have this treasure in jars of clay to show that the surpassing power belongs to God and not to us.

Jars of clay. Fragile. Cracked. Ordinary. But carrying something extraordinary.

That is you. That is me. We are not the treasure. We carry it. And the cracks are how the light gets out.

Three weeks done. You are in the home stretch.

Heather

subject: Day 22: Freedom
body:
Good morning.

You finish Second Corinthians today and then read all of Galatians. And Galatians is about one thing. Freedom.

Paul is furious. People are telling the Galatian Christians that they need to follow the Jewish law to be saved. And Paul says no. Absolutely not. Christ set you free. Do not go back to slavery.

It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery.

That verse changed my life. Because I am really good at putting chains back on myself that God already removed.

Nine days left.

Heather

subject: Day 23: Who you are in Christ
body:
Good morning.

Three letters today. Ephesians, Philippians, and Colossians. They are short. They are powerful. And they all answer the same question. Who are you now that you belong to Christ?

Ephesians says you are chosen, adopted, sealed, and seated with Christ. Philippians says you can do all things through Christ who strengthens you. Colossians says Christ is before all things and in Him all things hold together.

Philippians was written from prison. And it is the most joyful book in the New Testament. Paul says the word joy or rejoice sixteen times in four chapters. From a jail cell.

Joy is not about circumstances. It never has been.

Eight days left.

Heather

subject: Day 24: Letters to friends and a young pastor
body:
Good morning.

Thessalonians is Paul writing to a church he loves about the return of Jesus. He is answering their questions. What happens to the people who have already died? When is Jesus coming back?

And his answer is essentially, I do not know when. But I know He is. So live ready.

First Timothy is Paul writing to a young pastor he mentored. It is personal. Practical. Don't let anyone look down on you because you are young. Fight the good fight. Guard what has been entrusted to you.

If you are a leader, or raising one, First Timothy will speak to you today.

One week left.

Heather

subject: Day 25: Paul's last letter and a one-page masterpiece
body:
Good morning.

Second Timothy is Paul's last letter. He is in prison. He knows he is going to die. And he writes to Timothy one final time.

I have fought the good fight. I have finished the race. I have kept the faith.

That is how Paul says goodbye. Not with regret. Not with fear. With confidence that he did what he was called to do.

Titus is short and practical. And Philemon is one page. One single page about a runaway slave named Onesimus. Paul asks his friend to take Onesimus back, not as a slave but as a brother. It is the gospel in miniature.

Six days to go.

Heather

subject: Day 26: The Old Testament finally makes sense
body:
Good morning.

Hebrews ties everything together. If you have ever wondered what the Old Testament sacrifices and priests and temples were all about, Hebrews is the answer. They were all pointing to Jesus.

Chapter 11 is the faith hall of fame. By faith Abraham left everything. By faith Moses chose suffering over comfort. By faith Rahab welcomed the spies. These are real people who trusted God when they could not see the outcome.

And chapter 12 says you are surrounded by this great cloud of witnesses. Every person you read about this month is cheering you on.

Five days left. You are almost there.

Heather

subject: Day 27: Faith that does something
body:
Good morning.

James does not mess around. Faith without works is dead. Do not just listen to the word. Do what it says. Control your tongue. Care for the poor. Be patient.

James is the most practical book in the New Testament. It is faith with its sleeves rolled up.

First Peter is about hope in the middle of suffering. Written to people who were being persecuted for their faith. And Peter says, do not be surprised. But do not lose hope either.

Second Peter is about holding onto the truth when everything around you is trying to pull you away.

Four more days.

Heather

subject: Day 28: Love. That is the whole thing.
body:
Good morning.

John, the disciple who called himself the one Jesus loved, writes three short letters. And the theme is love.

God is love. If we love one another, God lives in us. There is no fear in love. Perfect love drives out fear.

After all the theology and the history and the letters and the arguments, it comes down to this. Love God. Love people. That is the whole thing.

Jude is one chapter. A warning to hold onto your faith. Short and fierce.

Three days left. You are about to finish the New Testament.

P.S. I do not want to lose this momentum. In August I am doing something different. One Book Deep. We will read the book of James every single day for 31 days. Same book, 31 times. Plus a daily prayer focus and a journal to write what God is saying. Depth instead of speed. If you want in, sign up at heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james

Heather

subject: Day 29: The beginning of the end
body:
Good morning.

Revelation. The last book of the Bible. And it is unlike anything else you have read.

Do not try to decode every symbol. Do not try to build a timeline. Just read it. Let the images wash over you. The throne room. The lamb. The scrolls. The worship.

Because before Revelation gets to the scary parts, it starts with worship. Chapter 4 and 5 are the most magnificent picture of heaven in all of Scripture. Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is to come.

That is where the story is heading. Not chaos. Worship.

Two more days.

P.S. August starts in two days. One Book Deep. Read James every day for 31 days. Pray with intention. Journal what God is saying. Sign up at heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james

Heather

subject: Day 30: Hold on. Almost there.
body:
Good morning.

This is the hardest stretch of Revelation. Seals and trumpets and bowls and beasts. It is intense.

But here is what I want you to hold onto today. In the middle of all of it, there are moments of worship. Moments where the story pauses and the heavens sing. The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever.

The darkness in Revelation is not the point. The darkness is the backdrop for the light.

One more day. Tomorrow you finish.

P.S. Tomorrow is the last day of July, but August starts the day after. One Book Deep. James. 31 days. Depth instead of speed. I would love to have you. heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james

Heather

subject: Day 31: You did it.
body:
Good morning.

This is it. The last day. The last chapters.

Today you will read about the fall of Babylon, the return of Jesus, and the new heaven and the new earth. And the Bible ends with this.

He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away. He who was seated on the throne said, I am making everything new.

That is how the story ends. Not with destruction. With restoration. Not with tears. With every tear wiped away.

You just read the entire New Testament in 31 days.

I do not know what stood out to you most. I do not know which verse stopped you in your tracks or which story you cannot stop thinking about. But I know something happened this month. God's Word does not come back empty.

Thank you for doing this with me. Thank you for showing up for 31 days. I am so proud of you.

P.S. Tomorrow is August 1st. And I am not done. One Book Deep starts tomorrow. We are going to read the book of James every single day for 31 days. Same book, 31 times. Plus a daily prayer focus and a journal where you write what God is saying. It is a completely different kind of challenge. Depth instead of speed. I would love to keep going with you. Sign up at heatherlynwilson.com/challenge-james

With love,
Heather
